  • %CPU - CPU Time as a percentage of Elapsed Time
  • %IO - User I/O Time as a percentage of Elapsed Time

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 4.02 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is 4.02 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the SELECT statement with SQL_ID
      "0asu682bpqmqq".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 0asu682bpqmqq.
         SELECT CHANNEL, COUNT(*) CNT, SUM(AMOUNT) TOTAL FROM
         BANK.TRANSACTIONS WHERE TXN_TS >= :B2 AND TXN_TS < :B1 AND STATUS =
         'POSTED' GROUP BY CHANNEL
   Rationale
      The SQL statement executed in container PERF with database ID
      3122828995.
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 100% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "0asu682bpqmqq" was executed 5846 times and
      had an average elapsed time of 0.081 seconds.
   Rationale
      Top level calls to execute the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID
      "1bpfvsqdnttyy" are responsible for 100% of the database time spent on
      the SELECT statement with SQL_ID "0asu682bpqmqq".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 1bpfvsqdnttyy.
         BEGIN bank.wl_monthly('05-partitioning/2-after-monthly', 120); END;


Finding 2: Large number of database connections
Impact is 4.02 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
A large number of sessions connected to the database instance were detected.
It can cause CPU oversubscription and consequently a severe degredation in
database performance and stability.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 4.02 active sessions, 100% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Reduce the number of sessions connected to the database instance. The
      number of connections to the database instance should not exceed ten
      times the number of CPU cores available to the database instance. It
      should also not exceed ten times the CPU limit assigned by the resource
      manager.
   Rationale
      There were 143 sessions connected to the database instance during the
      analysis period. This is a large number compared to the 2 CPU cores
      available to the database instance.


Finding 3: CPU Usage
Impact is 1.07 active sessions, 26.68% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Host CPU was a bottleneck and the instance was consuming 95% of the host CPU.
All wait times will be inflated by wait for CPU.
Host CPU consumption was 99%.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 3.75 active sessions, 93.18% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time on CPU. For example, the SELECT statement with SQL_ID
      "0asu682bpqmqq" is responsible for 100% of CPU usage during the analysis
      period.

   Recommendation 2: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.07 active sessions, 26.68% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider adding more CPUs to the host or adding instances serving the
      database on other hosts.
   Action
      Also consider using Oracle Database Resource Manager to prioritize the
      workload from various consumer groups.


Finding 4: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is .31 active sessions, 7.7% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.

   No recommendations are available.


Finding 5: Unusual "Other" Wait Event
Impact is .09 active sessions, 2.26% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "Failed Logon Delay" in wait class "Other" was consuming
significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .09 active sessions, 2.26% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "Failed Logon Delay" waits. Refer to
      Oracle's "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
